stories.title: Arrest as gardaí investigate death of man in Leitrim
stories.summary: A man in his 30s has been arrested in connection with the death of a man in Co Leitrim last night. The man, who was aged in his 40s, was found unresponsive following reports of an incident at a house in Arderry, near Carrigallen, shortly after 9pm. He was treated at the scene by emergency services but pronounced dead a short time later. Gardaí say they are investigating "all the circumstances" surrounding the man's death.

stories.title: EU Migration Pact overhauling asylum system now in effect
stories.summary: The EU Migration Pact comes into force today, two years after it was adopted by member states and the European Parliament. The pact overhauls existing EU rules to bring about what officials describe as a more efficient, streamlined system that will mean a departure from years of toxic politics around the issue. However, the pact has been criticised by both the far-right, for not going far enough, and by refugee organisations, who said its legal safeguards for those seeking protection are not sufficient. The Migration Pact follows years of torturous negotiations over how to manage the asylum system at EU level.

stories.title: Iran says no 'final conclusion' as Trump touts war deal
stories.summary: Iran has said it has not reached a final decision on a deal to end the war with the US, despite US President Donald Trump claiming an agreement could be signed in days and cancelling threatened strikes on Iran. Mr Trump's statements fuelled a stock market rally and tanked oil prices, again spurring hopes a resolution was nearing in the war triggered by US-Israeli strikes in February. Claiming that talks with Iran had been "brought to the highest level of Iranian leadership and approved," Mr Trump said he had "cancelled the scheduled strikes and bombings against Iran this evening." "Time and place of the signing to be announced shortly," he added.

stories.title: US-Canada bridge opening delayed after Trump objections
stories.summary: The US and Canada have decided to delay the opening of a new $4.7 billion bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor, Ontario, that was set to open in the coming days after US President Donald Trump earlier this year threatened to block the crossing. A formal ribbon-cutting had been planned for today for the Gordie Howe International Bridge, according to invitations seen by Reuters. "Canada and the United States have agreed to delay the opening of the bridge, taking the necessary time to resolve any outstanding issues," the Windsor-Detroit Bridge Authority said. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada agreed to delay the opening at the request of the Trump administration.

stories.title: 'As huge as JFK' - Mayo village prepares for Carney visit
stories.summary: The village of Aughagower in Co Mayo is preparing to welcome Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney this weekend. Mr Carney is due to travel to the homeplace of his paternal grandparents on Sunday. The trip forms part of a two-day visit to Ireland, which will include a stop-off in Dublin tomorrow. Mr Carney's grandparents, Robert Carney and Nora Moran, grew up around Aughagower and emigrated in July 1925 to begin a new life in North America.
